item.title: Haryana proposes FAR up to 264% for residential plots, S+4 height limit
item.description: The Haryana government is initiating amendments to the Haryana Building Code, which would enhance construction opportunities. Under the proposed changes, residential plots of up to 250 square metres would be eligible for a maximum floor area ratio of 264%. This modification is intended to assist homeowners wishing to remodel or expand their homes, as well as help developers.

item.title: Delhi government notifies new slum rehabilitation policy to house five lakh families
item.description: The Delhi government has unveiled a transformative slum rehabilitation policy targeting the provision of permanent homes for families in need. This progressive initiative is set to benefit around 5 lakh families living in qualifying settlements prior to January 1, 2025. Families will receive 1-BHK units equipped with essential amenities, enhancing their quality of life.

item.title: Telangana government expands Indiramma Towers housing project to four more cities
item.description: The Telangana government has announced the development of the Indiramma Towers across four cities: Nizamabad, Warangal, Nalgonda, and Karimnagar. Designed to cater to low-income families, these towers will feature one ground floor and five additional levels. The initial phase allocates 4.5 lakh homes, with construction currently underway for 1.9 lakh units and plans for an extra 2.

item.title: Over 2.2 lakh property cards issued, as Punjab government steps up drive
item.description: The Mera Ghar Mere Naam scheme in Punjab has seen the distribution of more than 2.2 lakh property cards to 1,377 villages. The project’s first phase is expected to finish by November 15, while the second phase is anticipated by the end of the month. This initiative not only helps residents acquire legal ownership but also resolves boundary disputes with advanced drone surveys and on-the-ground verification.

item.title: Delhi development body registers 80% growth in housing sales during April-October 2026
item.description: The Delhi Development Authority reported selling 9,332 flats during the initial seven months of financial year 2026-27. This figure represents an 80 percent increase compared to the same period last year. Narela has significantly contributed to these sales, accounting for over 90 percent of total sales in the current year. DDA plans to extend booking periods for various housing schemes until December 31, 2026.

item.title: Dhauli Heights allottees object to ‘conditional’ handover of keys
item.description: Members of the Dhauli Heights Association of Allottees are expressing frustration over the unexpected delays in receiving flat possession and keys. They argue that the Odisha Cooperative Housing Corporation is enforcing unreasonable conditions to get access to their homes. The association highlights that varying agreements are being drawn up due to ongoing legal issues among different allottees.

item.title: Chandigarh housing board opens six-month window for old GPA property transfers
item.description: Chandigarh Housing Board has made a significant move by approving a six-month extension of the property transfer policy specifically for General Power of Attorney transactions. This initiative aims to help property buyers from before 2011 who haven’t managed to complete their registrations. Those eligible can now establish formal ownership with necessary paperwork, along with a proposed one-time interest waiver of Rs 20 crore benefiting around 14,000 individuals.

item.title: Tamil Nadu housing board steps out of old blocks, decides to build gated communities in Chennai
item.description: The Tamil Nadu Housing Board plans to launch a project for the construction of 416 residential flats at three strategic sites in Chennai. This ambitious venture aims to provide high-income, rental, and mixed-income housing while optimizing land utilization. The flats will incorporate essential amenities, community spaces, and innovative building management systems, complete with effective parking solutions designed by leading architectural firms to enhance spatial and resource efficiency.

item.title: About 600 dilapidated housing board homes in Aishbagh to be demolished on November 14
item.description: Residents of the 600 dilapidated EWS houses in Aishbagh face a significant deadline. They must vacate their homes by November 13 to make way for a demolition drive by the Madhya Pradesh Housing Board, scheduled for November 14. Only those who are the original legal allottees are eligible for rental assistance and will be provided larger new flats, while unauthorized occupants will be evicted without any benefits.

item.title: Jaipur development body eases approvals for plots freed from power line curbs
item.description: In a bid to simplify procedures for plot owners, the Jaipur Development Authority has introduced a notification enabling applications for approvals and lease deeds to be processed locally. This transition comes on the heels of high-tension lines being removed from multiple colonies, marking an end to the delays that plagued applicants. The revamped approach promises to provide greater efficiency and support for numerous affected stakeholders.

item.title: Telangana housing board to hold online lottery for Indiramma Towers beneficiaries on November 3
item.description: On November 3, the Telangana housing board is set to host an online lottery to select beneficiaries for Indiramma Towers. A follow-up mop-up lottery will take place on November 4 to allocate any remaining vacant units from earlier rounds. The e-lottery aims to provide transparency, with live social media broadcasts allowing the public to witness the process.

item.title: Bhubaneswar development body amends Ekamra Residency project to comply with RERA regulations
item.description: The Bhubaneswar Development Authority has introduced crucial changes to the Ekamra Residency housing project's regulations. Notable adjustments include shortening the refund period for earnest money deposits from 60 days to 45 days. Additionally, the interest on late payments will now reference the State Bank of India's lending rate instead of a previously fixed rate.

item.title: OC amnesty scheme in Mumbai sees poor response; less than 10 applications filed in nearly two months
item.description: Nearly 19,000 buildings in Mumbai are reportedly operating without Occupation Certificates as a civic amnesty scheme continues. The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation launched this scheme to assist eligible property owners. Despite widespread need, fewer than ten applications have been submitted since its initiation. A public seminar has been organized to clarify the scheme's provisions for housing societies and individual owners.

item.title: Bhubaneswar development body extends Ekamra Residency application deadline to November 30
item.description: Bhubaneswar Development Authority has announced a one-month extension for applications to the Ekamra Residency project. This initiative seeks to boost participation from eligible homebuyers amid concerns over affordability, given that only under 200 applications have been filed for the 496 flats. The authority plans to ramp up its outreach strategies to better connect with prospective buyers during this extended timeframe.

item.title: Pharma company Gufic buys duplex apartment in Mumbai’s Juhu for over ₹236 crore
item.description: Gufic has made a significant real estate purchase with the acquisition of a luxury apartment in Mumbai. The duplex is located in the upscale Lodha Avalon project on Juhu Tara Road, featuring 19,694 square feet of space. This transaction, valued at Rs 236.33 crore, highlights the ongoing demand for luxury residential properties in the city. The purchase also involved a considerable stamp duty of Rs 14.18 crore for registration.

item.title: Property registrations in Mumbai rise 9% to 12,690 units in October 2026: Knight Frank
item.description: In October 2026, Mumbai saw a surge in property registrations, hitting 12,690 units, which reflects a nine percent increase from the previous year. Alongside this, stamp duty collections rose to ₹1,173 crore, compared to ₹1,040 crore last October. From January to October 2026, total registrations reached 1,32,040, a seven percent rise from 2025.

item.title: Over 270 Agartala slum residents get flats under affordable housing scheme
item.description: The Agartala Light House Project has delivered flat allotments to 278 lower-income families after an eight-year wait. This transformative initiative focuses on providing affordable housing in accordance with the GHTC-India scheme. The project features approximately 1,000 modern flats, constructed using innovative technologies for improved durability and efficiency, while also incorporating essential amenities like healthcare and community centers.

item.title: Supertech homebuyers move SC as 17 stalled projects remain stuck, ₹30 crore spent
item.description: Homebuyers of Supertech Limited have raised significant concerns regarding the lack of progress on stalled housing projects. The Homebuyers’ Association alleges that funding for the projects has been repeatedly declined, despite available proposals. The Association urges the Supreme Court to appoint a One-Man Committee for project completion. They emphasize the financial burden on homebuyers due to growing expenses without any delivered units.

item.title: Delhi government extends cut off date for registration of properties in unauthorised colonies
item.description: The Delhi government has announced a new deadline for residents to secure ownership rights in unauthorized colonies, moving the date to January 31 from the original October 31. This decision comes in response to the unexpectedly low application rate. Concerns over taxes and responsibilities related to ownership are prevalent among residents. Under the PM-UDAY scheme, legal rights will be extended to individuals living in 1,511 unauthorized colonies.

item.title: Mangaluru development body eases land approvals, cuts regularisation fee to 1%
item.description: Mangaluru's property owners rejoice! New government measures have significantly reduced regularisation fees for unauthorised land subdivisions and simplified the approval process for both old and new subdivisions. The necessity for separate land conversion orders in Muda’s master plan has been lifted. To enhance clarity, a public helpdesk is being established at the Muda office, designed to facilitate a smoother approval experience for property owners.
